alcance: 101 rural schools and 500 urban-marginal schools targeted for computers, internet access, and VSAT antennas
notas: Launched from a school in Huacrapuquio, Junin, deliberately outside Lima. Widely criticised for prioritising hardware delivery over actual connectivity infrastructure and teacher training.
imagenAlt: Scanned 2003 Caretas magazine article discussing Plan Huascaran

programa: National Fibre-Optic Backbone (Red Dorsal Nacional de Fibra Optica)
entidad: Ministry of Transport and Communications (MTC) / Azteca Comunicaciones Peru
alcance: Over 13,000 km of fibre-optic cable, concession contract signed in 2014 for USD 333 million
notas: Established by Law No. 29904 (2012), regulated by Supreme Decree No. 014-2013-MTC. The physical backbone that later made rural broadband programmes possible.
citation: Congreso de la Republica del Peru, 2012; Ministerio de Transportes y Comunicaciones, 2013

alcance: Over 3.8 million people connected across more than 19,000 rural localities, 2,700+ 4G stations
notas: Symbolically launched on 28 June 2019 with a live video call between Moya (Junin) and Atalaya (Ucayali), connecting an Andean town with an Amazonian one for the first time.
citation: Telefonica, 2019; BID Invest, 2020; Internet para Todos, n.d.
imagenAlt: Launch event of Internet para Todos in Moya, Junin

programa: Pronatel EPAD (Espacios Publicos de Acceso Digital)
entidad: Ministry of Transport and Communications (MTC) / Pronatel
alcance: First 362 rural public squares connected, expanded in May 2021 to 223 rural localities across four regions, benefiting over 180,000 people
notas: Provides free WiFi in rural public squares, reaching areas without commercial cafes or shopping centres.

alcance: 252 towns connected via 2,800 km of fibre optic and 224 free public WiFi spaces, benefiting over 141,000 people, including 268 schools, 121 health posts, and 53 police stations
notas: An active, ongoing project at the time of writing, showing the rural digital-divide effort is still in progress.
